prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1026; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and reported a wrist injury along with vehicle damage to the rear of the claimant's car.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which lists the claimant's vehicle as struck from behind while stopped. The insured driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account matching the claimant's description of the impact. Photos from the scene were received and show damage consistent with a rear impact.

Entry 4: Contacted the two witnesses listed on the report. Both confirmed the collision happened as described, and the responding officer's notes state the claimant was not inside the vehicle when the crash occurred, which needs to be reconciled with the claimant's statement.

Entry 5: Claimant gave a recorded statement describing the collision and the wrist injury. The account was consistent with what was said during the initial phone call.

Entry 6: Obtained an appraisal of the vehicle. The damage pattern lines up with the reported impact, and no prior damage to the rear of the car is known from our records or the appraiser's inspection.

Entry 7: Received the medical records for the wrist fracture. The injury is the type expected from a collision of this force, and no prior injury to that area appears in the records provided.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy tapering as the claimant's range of motion improved. Nothing in the file suggests a gap in coverage timing or pre-existing damage that would change the assessment.

Entry 9: Reviewed the full file and the discrepancy regarding the claimant's position at impact is noted for follow-up. All other elements of the claim are consistent, and the file is being routed to the supervisor for a coverage and liability decision.
